definition: A pedagogical agent is a concept borrowed from computer science and artificial intelligence and applied to education, usually as part of an intelligent tutoring system (ITS).
details: It is a simulated human-like interface between the learner and the content, in an educational environment. A pedagogical agent is designed to model the type of interactions between a student and another person. Mabanza and de Wet define it as "a character enacted by a computer that interacts with the user in a socially engaging manner". A pedagogical agent can be assigned different roles in the learning environment, such as tutor or co-learner, depending on the desired purpose of the agent. "A tutor agent plays the role of a teacher, while a co-learner agent plays the role of a learning companion".

explainer.lead: A simulated human-like interface between learner and content, usually part of an intelligent tutoring system. It matters because it models the social interactions of learning rather than only delivering material.

tiers.eli5: It is a computer character that acts like a tutor or a fellow student, talking with you while you learn.
tiers.practitioner: Designers assign the agent roles such as tutor or co-learner depending on the learning goal. A pitfall is that a socially engaging character does not by itself guarantee better learning outcomes.
tiers.paperLevel: Mabanza and de Wet define a pedagogical agent as 'a character enacted by a computer that interacts with the user in a socially engaging manner'; it can take roles such as tutor or co-learner in the learning environment.

explainer.example: An intelligent tutoring system presents a friendly on-screen character that asks a student guiding questions and offers hints, acting in the tutor role.
